free_tier.stated: The bot's page: 'Fast and safely collect files from Telegram with up to 10TB Private Cloud. Full support for torrent, magnet and more.' 25 096 monthly users. The 10 TB is the paid tier: PikPak's help centre says 'Free accounts include 6 GB of storage, and Premium includes 10 TB.'
free_tier.notes: 6 GB free storage; 3 cloud-download tasks a day on a free account

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap is stated for the bot. The binding free limits are the 6 GB account store and 'three Cloud Download tasks per day'.

retention.stated: Files stay in the PikPak account until deleted or until the account lapses; a free account has 6 GB, so retention of a large library is a paid feature.

egress.terms: Downloading out of PikPak is metered per account: 'Free PikPak accounts have a daily Downstream limit of 20 GB, which resets at 0:00 Singapore Time. All Connected Apps together can use up to 25% of this daily limit, or 5 GB per day.' Upgrading to Premium removes that limit.
egress.free_allowance: 20 GB/day downstream on a free account

interface_detail: A Telegram chat that acts as a remote control for a PikPak account. The file moves Telegram -> PikPak, so Telegram is the source and PikPak the store.
tooling: Any Telegram client. Forwarding a channel post or sending a magnet/HTTP/Twitter/TikTok link is the whole interface.
chaining: Sweeps files and magnets out of Telegram into a 6 GB free cloud store with a 20 GB/day egress meter; the reverse of a Telegram-as-drive path, and the only hosted bot found that moves bytes out of Telegram at scale.

limits.value: 6 GB stored on a free account
3 cloud-download tasks/day on a free account
20 GB/day downstream on a free account; connected apps 5 GB/day

binding_note: 6 GB of storage fails first: a 1 TiB month cannot be stored on a free account at all, and the 3-task/day count fails alongside it.

identity_cost.detail: PikPak registration is by email: 'An email address for registration and verification... No credit card is needed to start the basic free plan.' The bot then needs the account linked.

reliability_note: Free accounts are metered on both storage and downstream; reaching either daily or monthly connected-app limit slows traffic to about 100 KB/s rather than failing it.
confidence_note: Bot description and user count from t.me; every number from PikPak's own help centre and FAQ. The mapping 'bot transfer counts as a cloud download task' is inferred, not stated.
